decisions.reason: The comma preserves the 어디로, 어떻게 listing; dropping it is no real prose gain.
그리다 is the spearhead tracing a semicircle; “swept through” changes the motion.
A quoted cry is the natural English for a vocalization; a leading dash reads as leftover System UI.
주춤거리다 is a physical falter in the retreat, not just hesitation.
Same as H003: quoted roar rather than a dashed UI line.
SOL adds an unsupported “It” to the System notice; BASE keeps the announcement voice.
“A frame” is translationese for 덩치; SOL recasts size, mace, and roar without losing facts.
이야기가 다르죠 is the idiom “a different story”; SOL flattens it to “This is different.”
든가 is a sarcastic prompt, not a genuine question; the period keeps the challenge.
해 드려요 is a sarcastic offer (“would you like me to”), and … is the house ellipsis.
“Suffered internal injuries” and “I’d rather fight the monsters” match 내상 / 차라리 … 낫지 without calque.
한 마디 is a single remark; “one last” is not in the source.
처맞는 말 is the compact 맞는/처맞는 pun; SOL explains the joke.
그리고…… is a narrative beat; “And then…” carries it, “And…” is clipped.
The comma is unnecessary in this spoken line; the question reads cleaner without it.
밀려오고 있다 is an ongoing surge; SOL’s simple past drops the progressive.
“Working as a Hunter” and “shining brightly” are more natural; 적힌 is already implied by the Status Window line.
이 이상 is degree (“any further”), not duration (“any longer”).
SOL flattens 또 다른 내가 지금 이곳에 있었다 into a generic “no longer the same.”
Same as H003: quoted vocalization.
The participle “casting a shadow” is tighter and equivalent to 그림자를 드리운.
Captures 창날의 끝 (“tip”) and puts “opened” in natural English order.
감싸 안은 is the fog wrapping the wetlands; “hung over” is a different image.
“Including the boss” is the natural English order for 보스를 포함한.
They went together; 두엇 is “a couple”; SOL makes it Choi-only, adds “he had seen,” and over-specifies “two or three.”
거기에 더해 is “on top of that,” not a fresh “and then there was.”
흥미로운 is “intriguing,” and “limits of this … man” is cleaner English.
English needs the object of 들키지; “about him” does not change the sense.
SOL drops 문득 (“suddenly”).
눈에 들어왔다 is “entered his vision”; “field of vision” pads it and “Then” weakens the linkage.
“Completely” intensifies 상반신이 날아간 without source support.
이거 / 비싼 건데 is present “this stuff’s expensive,” not past “this was.”
저런 인간 is dismissive “guy,” not “man”; use the English ellipsis.
decisions.replacement: …There was no way a guy like that could be.

decisions.reason: 고생하셨습니다 is formal thanks for labor, not a casual “Good work.”
이 40대 아저씨 is “this” man in front of him.
수고하셨어요 acknowledges Kim’s labor; “Thank you too” is a generic thanks.
“Divorced from reality” is the idiomatic rendering of 현실성 없는.
그는 is one of the church deacons, not Kim; “one of them” and “pay … as a tithe” fix the misread.
“At seven years old, I’d been…” is the natural syntax for 일곱 살이었던 나는.
그 말이 is “those words,” not a vague “That.”
다시 생각해 보니 is “thinking back on it,” not “thinking about it again.”
얇은 is light fabric, not skinny; 꼭 still needs “just like.”
decisions.replacement: Team Leader Choi had already changed into street clothes. In a lightweight tailored suit, he looked just like a celebrity.

decisions.reason: Merging the short question onto the attribution is natural English.
The question now lives in H043; the leftover line should go.
“Tomorrow?” already is the 되묻는다; “asked back” is redundant.
The question is about this coming weekend, not weekends as a general habit.
House style uses …, not the Korean …….
House-style ellipsis in the silent beat.
House-style ellipsis in the silent beat.
충격받은 얼굴로 물었다 is asking with a shocked look; “stared” changes the action.
“Throw in extra pay” is the English collocation for 얹어 주고.
인력 사무소 is a day-labor agency, not a proper-noun Manpower Office.
House-style ellipsis.
“No exception” makes the compliance sense of 마찬가지 clear in English.
Same 인력 사무소 rendering as H052.
눈빛 is a look, not an expression; leading with the lip-smack follows Korean order.
“Could afford to” carries the 될 텐데요 allowance without adding a new claim.
“Could jump out” matches 튀어나오려는 as an about-to-happen impulse.
Unmarked 노 in this boat metaphor reads naturally as “oars”; singular is no improvement.
“Time I’d spent in Murim” is the natural English for 무림에서의 시간.
Keep 같았다 (“like”); SOL’s “struggling” is not in 달리는.
decisions.replacement: Ever since my father died, my life had been like a car running uphill.

decisions.reason: 발을 떼면 is taking the foot off the pedal; “let up” / “as though” soften the image and the voice.
Same 인력 사무소 term; 그거 refers to going there, not rest in general.
아, 네 here is accepting the order to rest, not confirming a fact.
이렇게까지 억지로 and 이 인간 are “this hard” and “this guy Choi,” not a milder “like this” plus title.
감성 팔이 is an emotional appeal, not a sentimental one.
“His slaves” spells out what 노예 농장주 only analogizes; BASE keeps the mindset, not extra bodies.
“Preparations are complete” is the natural formal English for 준비 끝났습니다.
돌아왔다 is “was back from”; “had returned after” is stiffer than Taekyung’s narration.
말 is “word,” not “command.”
다가 is blink-then-thought, not “until”; merge the short question without SOL’s sequence change.
decisions.replacement: It looked like a box of tonic drinks. I just blinked at it, then a thought flashed through my head and I asked carefully, “Don’t tell me this is money?”

decisions.reason: The question is now in H071; drop the leftover line.
“I’d get it” matches the casual 알았거든; “I would” is stiffer with no gain.
받아 들었다 is physically taking the box, not “accepted.”
좋다 is “liked,” not the stronger “preferred.”
였나 is uncertainty; “maybe” captures yesterday-or-the-day-before.
BASE drops 가장; it is the most important part still left.
얼마 is a question; the line needs the question mark.
“More than the contract says” is natural English for 계약서보다 좀 더.
쌩하니 사라졌다 is vanishing in a flash, not merely speeding off.
그야말로 is “really”; SOL drops it and adds “all.”
“Bewildered” and “caught my eye” match 황당한 얼굴 / 눈에 들어온다; SOL is only a reshuffle.
찰나 is simultaneity; BASE’s “and” makes the flash and the buckling sequential.
눈앞이 밝아진다 is his vision brightening; “the world in front of me” is calqued.
방언 here is an ecstatic outburst (“speaking in tongues”), not literal dialect, and it pays off the church bit.
“Contained” / “meant” read more naturally than “was” / “so” for the bundle math.
English catches oneself, not one’s legs; “make a thud” matches 소리가 날 만큼.
Smoother equivalent of the paper lying under the bundles and lining the box.
A sheet “contained” the record; “had” is weaker for 기록되어 있었다.
“Right down to” carries the extent in 까지.
“Last” and “final” are interchangeable here; no reason to swap.
SOL adds “echoed in my mind” and drops 떠나며 (“as he left”).
Must match Choi’s wording from H079.
일어났다 is getting up from his knees; “in the distance” duplicates 저 멀리.
decisions.replacement: I rose on trembling legs. Far off, the car’s lights were already fading.
